problem_statement: The CPU frequency scaling subsystem has no mechanism to constrain the highest-performance P-state based on temperature. A load-based policy can keep requesting the highest-performance P-state even when the die temperature is too high, risking thermal runaway. The subsystem should support an optional thermal cap layer that, based on configurable temperature trip points (with hysteresis), limits the maximum allowed P-state. When a temperature trip is active, the policy-selected P-state should be clamped to the cap P-state or lower (by index). Multiple active trips should apply the most restrictive cap. If the temperature sensor fails repeatedly, a fail-safe P-state (the lowest-performance one) should be applied. Recovery from sensor failure should recompute the cap from the next successful sample. The thermal cap should not raise a requested P-state that is already lower-performance than the cap.
